about.title: Sonoma Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Sonoma is a small town of about 11,000 people, and when a family here loses someone, neighbors notice. In 2025, public records list 41 injury collisions inside the city, 51 people hurt, and no traffic deaths. Still, crashes on Broadway, W Napa Street, or Rt 12 are only one way a life can end too soon; falls on someone else's property, medical errors, unsafe products, and workplace incidents also lead to wrongful death claims. In California, this is a civil action, separate from any criminal case. Standing goes first to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Losses that can be recovered include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive connects Sonoma County families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can explain where you fit before anyone files paperwork.

items.title: Attention to the two-year deadline
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks when a city, county, or state agency is involved. An early conversation helps protect that timeline.

items.title: A civil path that does not wait on a criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is separate from any prosecution and can move forward on its own. It seeks compensation for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance.

items.question: Sonoma recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death claims here are rare?
items.answer: Traffic deaths are only one category. Families in Sonoma also lose loved ones to falls, medical negligence, defective products, and workplace incidents, and a fatal crash on Rt 12 or another road just outside city limits still involves Sonoma residents. If negligence played a role, the claim exists regardless of what the citywide numbers show.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, with a different standard of proof. Waiting for a criminal verdict can eat into the two-year filing deadline, so it is worth speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it cost anything to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
